speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Prime Minister whether and, if so, how has the Ministry been working with family offices in Singapore to deepen investments in local companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
text: These include "Deal Fridays", FinTech Investor sessions, and the Singapore Week of Innovation and Technology (SWITCH), which we will be organising from 25-28 October, this month.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
text: We are also encouraging match-ups during the annual Singapore FinTech Festival, which will also be organised very shortly, from 2-4 November.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
text: At the same time, we must recognise that family offices come to Singapore to access investment and philanthropic opportunities in the broader Asian region.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (on behalf of the Prime Minister)
text: This adds to Singapore’s status as a dynamic as well as purposeful financial centre, supporting growth and opportunity in our neighbouring countries.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Deputy Speaker, I would like to thank the Minister of State for his reply.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The first is, how have and will local companies and the local workforce benefit from family offices?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Second, where do these family offices generally come from?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: That is, which country or which industry were they operating in before they set up in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The SFOs generate employment in Singapore in a couple of ways.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The first is by directly employing advisers and investment professionals; and also, to generate indirect employment when they work, for example, with external finance, tax and legal professionals, and also fund administrators, for example, custodians, on investment management, wealth planning and also operational matters.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, a wide aspect in both direct as well as indirect employment.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: SFOs also expand the pool of patient capital for Singapore-based startups and business ventures, as well as Singapore-based funds that invest in such companies.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Investee companies may also benefit from the strategic guidance offered by the principals of these family offices, many of whom themselves are owners of successful businesses.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Some families also use their SFOs or related entities to manage their investments and contributions towards social and philanthropic activities or causes in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regard to the second supplementary question on where the SFOs originate from, the SFO community in Singapore is diverse, it is international.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They come from a variety of regions, including Europe, the US as well as Asia.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And families who are keen to set up a satellite presence here in Singapore, do so because of our favourable business environment, connectivity to the region which allow for them to use Singapore as a base to explore investment opportunities beyond Singapore to the region.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I will also just share a little bit about what we are doing to attract these family offices, as related to that supplementary question.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Second is to develop the capabilities and to build essential skillsets among our service providers, both local as well as foreign, and our professionals.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, the Wealth Management Institute and the SMU Business Families Institute have launched a series of training programmes for family office advisers, professionals and principals that are then accredited against these skill maps.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, if there are many individuals or professionals who are interested in entering this space or to deepen your capabilities, you can also take reference to these skill maps to better equip yourselves with the necessary skillsets to enter this industry.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The final point is that we have, as a posture, consistently welcomed a variety of financial and other capital investments into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We have welcomed individual companies that can contribute to Singapore's growth, create good jobs, regardless of where they are and regardless of their country of origin where they come from.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, we need to remain open, we need to remain connected to global investors to strengthen Singapore's value proposition to Asia and to be a key Asian node for high growth tech investment and tech companies to base here, to grow their patient capital, and then to grow and be a base for new and exciting industries, and ultimately, create good jobs for Singaporeans.
